newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes find floor, Brent paper weakens.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes find floor, Brent paper weakens.

text.p: North Sea spot crudes found a floor on Thursday but a persistent overhang of prompt November barrels kept up the pressure on Brent paper, traders said.

In a quiet wet market a Forties cargo due to load November 28-30 was said to have fetched Dated Brent +9 cents, about four cents firmer than trade earlier in the week but details could not be confirmed.
"Margins are looking good but we've still got an overhang so I don't think we're in for a significant upturn," said a trader.
Dec Brent paper was 12 cents firmer at $22.27 a barrel by 1802 GMT but intermonth spreads lost ground over the session.
The Nov/Dec contango deepened -- offered at -15 cents late -- and Dec/Jan was pegged at +26 cents after trading early at +32 cents.
Jan/Feb also slipped a couple of cents from early trade at +42 cents to +38/+43 cents, dealers said.

A major offered a Nov 15-17 Brent at Dec -50 cents, seven cents firmer than a deal on Wednesday and was considering whether to offer a Nov 22-24 cargo kept from the paper chains on Thursday. The other cargo turning wet was kept by Statoil.
Brent CFDs saw the most activity with next week's dates trading at Jan Brent -12 cents, equivalent to Dec -40/42 cents.
The following week fetched Dec Brent -39/-40 cents and the first two weeks of December saw active trade with Dec 2-6/9-13 rolls trading twice at +3 cents and once at +2 cents.
In the Mediterranean, the sour crude market was steady with Russian Urals seen holding onto recent gains after trading Wednesday at Dated Brent -86 cents cif Med up from Tuesday's -93/-95 cents.
Wednesday's level was heard repeated to the same buyer, a trade house, on Thursday but details could not be immediately confirmed.
